extra.message: User input from sqli.get('username') is directly interpolated into an f-string SQL query passed to cur.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., username=' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication or extract data.

User input from ssti.get('mathexp') is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string and then rendered via test.render(). An attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions (e.g., {{config}} or {{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()}}) to achieve remote code execution.

User input from lfi.get('filename') is passed directly to fetchfile() which calls open(name).read() without any path validation or sanitization. An attacker can read arbitrary files on the server using directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../../etc/passwd).

User input from rfi.get('imagelink') is passed directly to requests.get(url=name) without URL validation or restriction. An attacker can make the server issue HTTP requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, enabling SSRF to access internal services, metadata endpoints, etc.

The value of the Host request header is read from request.headers['Host'] and reflected unsanitized into an HTML anchor tag: <a href='{h}'>. An attacker can inject a malicious Host header to perform HTTP header injection or reflected XSS by breaking out of the href attribute.

User input from xss.get('username') is reflected directly in the JSON response as f'Hello, {username}' without any HTML encoding or sanitization. If the response is rendered as HTML by a client, this enables reflected cross-site scripting.

Flask is started with debug=True, which enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger. This allows remote code execution via the debugger console if an attacker can trigger an exception and access the debugger PIN or when the PIN is calculable.

Hardcoded credentials are inserted into the USERS table: 'mike/kaines' on line 25 and 'admin/admin' on line 28. These credentials are embedded in source code and use weak passwords (admin/admin), making them easily discoverable and exploitable.

requests.get() is called with verify=False, which disables SSL certificate verification. This makes the outgoing HTTP requests vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing attackers to intercept or modify data in transit.
